rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.2-2.5 - two-year field experiment (2018-2020) in Yuanyang County with FI, DI and RF under three cropping systems, measured SWC, SNC, LAI, DM, yields, used to calibrate/validate WHCNS. Q2: Section 3.2 and Table 7 - DI irrigated 2H1Y, 3H2Y and 1H1Y received 34%, 36% and 40% less irrigation than FI over two years (water-meter-recorded amounts, Eq. 6), with seasonal savings of 31% for winter wheat and 40% for maize, while measured yields were maintained or higher (Table 6). Q4: Table 7 and Section 3.3 - the model simulated the intermediate water fluxes (soil evaporation lowered 8-74%, drainage 61-74%, runoff 37-49% under DI), and measured SWC (Fig. 2) was used to validate soil water dynamics. Q8: Section 4.4 - authors state drainage, evapotranspiration and runoff were not measured, so there are large uncertainties in simulated fluxes; observed data were limited and parameter sensitivity causes simulation uncertainty.
rows.notes: The review's attribution (34% for winter wheat, 36-40% for maize) slightly misreads the study: 34/36/40% are savings by cropping system (2H1Y/3H2Y/1H1Y); seasonal savings were 31% (wheat) and 40% (maize). The water-saving percentage is the difference in applied irrigation amounts (a treatment design quantity), not a measured outcome; evaporation/drainage/runoff reductions are model outputs only. Q3: no independent second method. Q5: single site/soil; wheat and maize only (summer and spring maize are one crop). Q6: 96 m2 plots. Q7: attribution of savings to small frequent applications is made via cited literature, not stated as a requirement. Q9: no dispersion reported for water-saving percentages or Table 7 fluxes (WUE in Table 6 does carry +/- values).

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.2-2.3 - own two-year randomized complete block field experiment with measured grain yields. Q2: Section 3.2 and Table 6, Fig. 4 - measured grain yields under DI were higher than FI in all cropping systems (e.g., 2H1Y annual average 19915 vs 18481 kg/ha; DI totals 39829 vs 36962 kg/ha over two years), with the order DI > FI > RF significant by ANOVA. Q4: Fig. 2 and Section 4.1 - measured SWC profiles showed FI gave excessive soil water while DI maintained SWC at optimum levels, linked by the authors to improved growth; soil evaporation and drainage also modelled (Table 7). Q8: Section 4.4 - authors state limitations of observed data and field management, and that unmeasured fluxes create large uncertainties in simulated N fates and crop yields. Q9: Table 6 - grain yields reported as mean +/- error for each crop season and annual average.
rows.notes: Yield differences between DI and FI for individual seasons were often small; Section 3.2 even states no significant difference between DI and FI within the same cropping system for some crops, while annual averages were significantly different. Q3: field yields and model simulation are not independent methods (model calibrated on these yields). Q5: single site and soil, two crops. Q6: plot scale only. Q7: no condition stated as a requirement for the yield effect.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.2-2.5 - own field experiment plus WHCNS model calibrated with year-1 and validated with year-2 measured SWC, SNC, LAI, DM and yields. Q2: Section 3.4 and Table 8 - simulated annual N leaching under DI was 58%, 62% and 59% lower than FI in 2H1Y, 3H2Y and 1H1Y (e.g., 46.5 vs 111.7 kg/ha in 2H1Y), with NH3 volatilization reduced 33-55%; Table 6 and Section 3.2 - NUE computed from measured yields was significantly higher under DI (e.g., 32.12 vs 26.46 kg/kg in 2H1Y); the model's SNC and SWC outputs were compared with field measurements (Table 3, Fig. 2-3). Q4: Table 7 and Table 8 - the model simulated drainage (the pathway for leaching), reduced 61-74% under DI, and measured soil mineral N profiles to 100 cm were used in calibration. Q8: Section 4.4 - authors explicitly state that N leaching, volatilization and denitrification were not measured, so there are large uncertainties in simulated N fates; more observed datasets are needed for calibration.
rows.notes: N leaching is a model output, not a measurement; it counts under Q2 only because the model was validated against measured SWC and SNC from the same plots, and the authors themselves flag large uncertainty in simulated N fates. The passage's causal framing (leaching reduced 'by improving NUE') is not tested; the study attributes lower leaching to smaller, more frequent water and fertilizer doses, citing other work. Q3: no independent second method (no lysimeter or resin measurement). Q5: one site/soil. Q6: plot scale. Q7: no requirement stated from own findings. Q9: no dispersion reported for N leaching values in Table 8 (NUE in Table 6 does carry +/- values, but the claimed effect is leaching).

notes: Full text appears complete. Study is a plot-scale field experiment (96 m2 plots, one sandy clay loam site in Henan) combined with the WHCNS model; measured variables were SWC, SNC, LAI, dry matter and grain yield, while all water and N flux outputs (evaporation, drainage, runoff, N leaching, volatilization, denitrification) are simulated and unmeasured, as the authors acknowledge in Section 4.4. Water-saving percentages derive from applied irrigation amounts set by the treatment design.
